answer: Latency-profile identity gating. Each identity must sustain a rhythm of small signed actions: inter-arrival timings and burst shapes are scored against an expected human-or-agent traffic curve. New identities from a cold tundra of no history start throttled until they match. Batch-registered sybils share a hollow, machine-regular cadence that the scorer flags. Persistent variance below threshold freezes the identity, as inert as shale. Attackers must pay real wall-clock time and jitter each sock puppet independently, making mass identity creation cost hours of pacing per account.
